outcome: Childhood overweight or obesity (age-sex-specific BMI ≥85th percentile)
cohort: 1441 racially and ethnically diverse mother-child dyads in the Boston Birth Cohort
finding: Both cesarean delivery and pre-pregnancy overweight/obesity were independently associated with childhood overweight or obesity, and the risk was highest in children born by cesarean delivery to obese mothers.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivered children had 1.4 times greater odds of becoming overweight or obese in childhood compared to vaginally delivered children.
birth_weight: Measured, but specific values not reported
